title: staggered-capacity-commit-ledger-na-eu-apac-24mo
body:
Capacity Commit Ledger — NA / EU / APAC (24-month rolling)

Executive summary:
- Purpose: A commit-led ledger to stagger GPU capacity onboarding across NA / EU / APAC to match inbound demand while preserving 15–30% operational buffer and enabling cross-region fallbacks.
- Horizon: 24 months (2026-04 through 2028-03). Plan uses quarterly activation windows and monthly monitoring triggers.
- Key outcome: flatten capital spend spikes, preserve latency SLOs in each region, and target steady-state aggregated utilization of 65–75%.

Key assumptions:
- Steady growth scenario: 35% YoY token volume growth; high-growth scenario reserves additional 20% optional commits in vendor windows.
- Preferred GPU SKUs: A800 / H100 equivalents depending on cloud vendor availability. Mix target: 60% A800-class (cost-sensitive), 40% H100-class (high-throughput).
- Buffer target: 20% operational buffer for NA/EU, 25% for APAC due to limited regional supply windows.
- Migration: New capacity takes 4–8 weeks from purchase commitment to first production-capable pool in hosted deployments; private deployments may add 6–12 weeks.
- Activation triggers: sustained 7-day rolling utilization >72% or lead indicators (reserved queue growth + warm-start misses) > threshold.

Notes on table: Cumulative_Units are per-region running totals for committed active units. Planned_Buffer_pct is the portion of committed capacity not expected to be used under normal conditions (operational/spare capacity). Target_Utilization_pct reflects the expected steady-state utilization after initial warm-up and placement optimizations.

Activation & rollout timeline (detailed milestones):
- Commit window A (contracts signed): 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-21 -> finance approval + vendor deposit.
- Provisioning window (cloud vendor onboarding): 2026-04-22 to 2026-05-21 -> infra config, VPC peering, subnet allocations.
- Canary and optimization: 2026-05-22 to 2026-06-10 -> internal traffic canary, KV cache priming.
- Production cutover: 2026-06-11 -> route 20% traffic first 72h, ramp to 100% over 7 days if stable.
- Repeat cadence each quarter with a 2-week readiness buffer between commit and provisioning windows for vendor delays.

Risk register (top-6 risks with mitigations):
1) Vendor supply shock (GPU SKU allocation shifts) -> Maintain SKU-flexible orders and a 15% cross-SKU contingency; pre-authorize alternative cloud provider swaps.
2) Port/shipping delays for dedicated on-prem/private -> Increase lead time assumptions to 12 weeks for private; pre-order long-lead items (racks, PDUs).
3) Sudden demand spike beyond buffer -> Short-term burst options: enable burst pools in other regions (multi-region routing) and throttle non-critical workloads.
4) Cost overrun from repeated H100 buys -> Introduce quarterly cost cap reviews and opt for mixed-mode quantized instances for experimental traffic.
5) Regulatory hold in EU -> Maintain a pool of EU-only pinned capacity and canary traffic that can be quickly isolated.
6) Networking peering failures -> Pre-validated cross-region failover routing and BGP route dampening policies; SRE periodic drills.

Vendor & procurement notes:
- Negotiate flexible cancellation windows on long-lead H100 reservations (aim for 60-day soft cancel).
- Ask vendors for staggered shipment commitments to match quarter windows, not single bulk arrivals.
- Include SLA credits for missed shipment dates above 10% of committed units per quarter.

Monitoring and alerts (operational playbook):
- Metrics to instrument: region_pool_util_pct, warm_start_miss_rate, reserved_queue_depth, avg_latency_p95, preemption_events_by_region.
- Alert thresholds (sample): region_pool_util_pct > 75% (warning), > 85% (pagable). reserved_queue_depth > 200 (warning). warm_start_miss_rate > 200/day (warning).
- Runbook actions: first-line throttle non-critical routing, second-line enable reserved burst pool in fallback region, third-line open procurement assistance channel.

Open action items (owners):
- Finalize multi-vendor pricing and cancellation terms (Owner: Daniel Kim) — due 2026-03-18.
- Implement monthly regional utilization dashboard with 7-day trendline (Owner: Sofia Rios) — due 2026-03-25.
- Add APAC freight window calendar to vendor tracker (Owner: Liam O'Connor) — due 2026-03-12.

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet is intentionally conservative on activation timing for APAC due to historical vendor frictions. Please flag any enterprise customers with contract cliffs in 2026–2027 so we can reprioritize NA commits.
- If finance wants a single-year view instead of 24 months, export CSV above and set filter to quarters Q2-2026 through Q1-2027.

Comments (working draft):
- Still need to align on preferred SKU mix for EU after benchmarking cold-start cost parity (SRE benchmarking tickets pending).
- Consider a small experimental pool (50–80 A800 units) in South America via multi-cloud for low-latency trials — separate addendum required.
